summary.intent: Assess whether GSD Phase 72 (SDK write-plane durability) needed discussion before planning, reconcile stale/missing todos across phases 70-73, then plan/execute/ship Phase 72 — work that was interrupted by discovering and fixing two real CI regressions (web-e2e, desktop-e2e) plus follow-on flakiness before resuming.
summary.outcome: Both CI regressions were root-caused and fixed (PR #601 FUSE seq-equivocation + driver fix, merged; PR #600 web floor-store fix + sdk-e2e idempotency fix + 4 web-e2e flake fixes, merged after full CI-equivalent local verification). Phase 72 was fully planned (10 plans/7 waves) and executed to completion with all Success Criteria met, plus an added hardening pass that fixed 113 pre-existing test-file TypeScript errors and wired test-inclusive typechecking into CI; verification/shipping was still in progress (resolving stale skipped tests) when the transcript ends.

repo: GSD todos are retired by moving pending/ files to completed/ (not a resolved/ folder, which stays empty) — checking the wrong directory gives a false 'nothing addressed' signal.

ci-e2e.yml (web-e2e + desktop-e2e) triggers only on push-to-main or workflow_dispatch, never on pull_request — PRs get no e2e signal unless manually dispatched via `gh workflow run <file> --ref <branch>` (the `-f ref=` input form is rejected with HTTP 422 on definitions predating that input).
sdk-e2e runs on pull_request via ci.yml, unlike web/desktop e2e.

Playwright's `ciFloor()` helper (tests/web-e2e/page-objects/file-browser/file-list.page.ts:10) raises wait timeouts to a 60s floor only under CI; local runs use much tighter caller-specified timeouts (15-30s), so IPNS-gated mutations that reliably pass in CI flake locally under load — local verification must run with `CI=1` (and a `reuseExistingServer` patch, since that flag is `!process.env.CI`) to be representative.

Root `pnpm typecheck` previously only ran each package's build (tsconfig.build.json, which excludes tests) — test files were never typechecked in CI, letting ~113 errors accumulate across 15 files (vitest v2→v3 Mock-generics drift plus Phase-62 retired-type fallout in sdk tests).

@cipherbox/* packages resolve cross-package types via the workspace symlink to built `dist` (no path aliases or TS project references) — a package's test-inclusive typecheck requires its upstream deps already built, so CI must build first then typecheck (interleaving isn't needed if builds already run in dependency order).

Phase 71 (#599) shipped with an anti-equivocation IPNS gate (rejects same-sequence republish with a different CID, 400) plus a full share-DTO field rename (readDescriptorRef→encryptedReadKey, rootIpnsName→shareRootIpnsName) — both broke shipped/test code that wasn't updated in the same PR (FUSE first-publish path, a desktop-e2e .mts driver, an sdk-e2e assertion).

Phase 70.1 collapsed two IndexedDB rotation stores (generation-high-water, seq-high-water) into one `rotation-floor` store (DB v2, keyed by nodeId) — test helpers referencing the old store names silently short-circuit and return undefined rather than erroring.
Local commits can appear to hang for ~2min due to a 1Password SSH-signing prompt (known issue) — verify via `git log` rather than assuming failure and retrying.

GSD plan:pre hook fragments are stored as raw (non-strict) JSON with literal control characters inside string values — `jq`/direct `JSON.parse` fail; a lenient parser escaping control chars only inside string literals is needed to extract them.

code.finding: publish_file_node hardcoded seq=1 on first-publish gated only by 'inode cid empty' — a stale/dropped UploadComplete re-triggers it with a fresh CID, colliding with Phase 71's anti-equivocation gate. Fixed by resolving IPNS before the seq-1 branch: NotFound→first-publish, Found→route into publish_with_cas_retry with the resolved seq.

publish_with_cas_retry gained an optional preresolved_seq param (per Greptile P2) so the Found path avoids a redundant second IPNS resolve on its first CAS attempt; conflict-retry path still always re-resolves since a pre-resolved value is stale after conflict.

ciFloor() (line 10) floors waits to 60s only under CI; waitForItemToDisappear (line 130) applies it — but writable-shares.spec.ts and full-workflow.spec.ts had several bare 15000/30000ms waits on the highest-latency (IPNS-gated) paths with no CI floor, causing local-only flakes that don't manifest in CI.

getWriteBodyParams (duplicated at client.ts and bin/index.ts) needed a fail-closed fix: on a genuine IPNS resolve null with a real (non-zero, 32-byte) writeKey present, throw naming the folder's ipnsName instead of silently sealing an empty write-body; the legitimate zero-writeKey read-only fallback path is untouched.

Test 21 (D-06 concurrent first-publish) asserted exactly one 200 + one 409, but Phase 71's same-CID idempotency legitimately allows two 200s when the loser serializes after the winner commits — rewritten to accept ≥1 fulfilled and all rejected reasons being 409.

workflow: When a subagent's summary and a raw `git`/`cat-file` check disagree, re-verify with a decisive direct check before trusting either — an earlier ad-hoc cat-file check in this session was simply buggy.

For unattended long-running phase execution on a pnpm monorepo, prefer sequential execution on the main tree over git-worktree isolation — fresh worktrees lack node_modules, a known failure mode, and heavily-serialized phases (all touching one file like client.ts) gain little from worktree parallelism anyway.

When a code-review bot (Greptile/CodeRabbit) finding is valid but low-value/high-blast-radius, it's reasonable to defer it as a follow-up todo rather than bundling into the current fix — but if the user explicitly asks to fix it now, verify all callers of the shared helper before widening its signature.

Capturing an unplanned-but-necessary side task (e.g. 'fix all test TS drift + wire CI') as a durable todo file immediately, before deep-diving, preserves it across context compaction and lets it be sequenced deliberately (here: as the final hardening plan) instead of derailing the current wave.

Local reproduction of CI-only flakes requires matching CI's actual timeout regime (CI=1), not just re-running locally — several rounds of 'fix one flake, hit a new one' were actually the same local/CI timeout-floor asymmetry surfacing at different call sites.

friction: Initially checked the wrong todo directory (resolved/, which is always empty) instead of completed/, requiring a user correction mid-turn.
`gh workflow run -f ref=` failed with HTTP 422 because the workflow definition predates that input; had to switch to `--ref <branch>`.

Local web-e2e verification cascaded through a chain of local-only timing flakes (4.10 batch delete, 4.11 batch move, 2.1 folder create) across ~6 background runs before a CI-equivalent (CI=1) run finally reached and validated the actual target fixes (6.6.2, 8.2) — each cascade wasted a ~5-11 minute run.

Setting CI=1 locally to match CI's timeout floor broke `reuseExistingServer` (tied to `!process.env.CI`), forcing a temporary playwright.config.ts patch (reverted after) to keep using the already-running dev stack.
GSD plan:pre hook JSON contains literal control characters in string values, breaking standard JSON parsing; required writing a custom lenient parser script.
Executor subagent sandboxes couldn't read `.env`, so several live sdk-e2e validations (bin-operations test, TEE gates) had to be deferred to phase-level verification where `.env` access works.

Discovered mid-execution that ~113 pre-existing test-file TypeScript errors (vitest v3 Mock-generics drift + Phase-62 retired-type fallout) had been silently accumulating because CI never typechecked test files — a scope surprise that required two dedicated fixer agents plus new CI wiring.

Near the end, discovered several tests still skipped with stale `TODO(phase 63)`/`TODO(phase 65)` markers even though phases 63 and 65 had already shipped — indicating skip-markers aren't being revisited as phases complete.
open_items: Resolving stale skipped sdk tests (TODO(phase 63)/TODO(phase 65) blocks, including one whose premise — moveItem re-encryption — was redesigned away) was in progress via a dedicated agent when the transcript ends; phase verification and /ship-phase 72 are still pending on this.
Deferred live validations from executor sandboxes (bin-operations sdk-e2e test, high-blast-radius walkChildWriteKey web-e2e run) still need to be run at phase verification per plan 72-05/72-08 notes.
Phase 73 planning/execution is queued to start only after Phase 72 is fully merged, per the user's stated plan→execute→ship-then-repeat flow.
